name: Sika MonoTop-723 N
paste:
SIKA MONOTOP®-723 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika MonoTop®-723 N, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/sika_monotop_-723n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika MonoTop®-723 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika MonoTop®-723 N is a polymer modified surfacing/finishing mortar, ready to mix, meeting the requirement of class R3 of EN 1504-3.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Thin layer render
    - Use as a concrete pore sealer / levelling mortar
    - Repairing of minor defects (pores and honeycombed concrete)
    - Suitable for restoration work (Principle 3, method 3.1 and 3.3 of EN 1504-9)
    - Suitable for preserving or restoring passivity (principle 7, method 7.1 and 7.2 of EN 1504-9)
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika MonoTop®-723 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: R3 Pore Sealer and Levelling Mortar
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Meets requirements of EN 1504-3
    - AS4020:2005 potable water approved
    - QLD TMR approval 2019
    5.34 Repair Materials (Concrete)- Mortars
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-3: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; listed under approvals, certificates or standards; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1); Characteristics / Advantages (p.1); Description (p.1); Technical Information > Reaction to fire (p.2).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - AS4020:2005: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - AS1012.9:2000: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - AS1012.17:2000: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1504: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: System Information > System structure (p.2).
    - EN 1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Important Considerations (p.3).
    - EN1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > SUBSTRATE QUALITY / PRE-TREATMENT (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy to apply and excellent finishing
    - Suitable for hand or wet spray application
    - Can be applied up to 5 mm thick per application layer
    - Class R3 of EN 1504-3
    - Restoration work
    - Sulphate resistant
    - Low cracking sensitivity
    - Very good resistance to water and chloride penetration
    - Compatible with Sikagard® overcoat systems
    - A1 fire rating
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Portland cement, selected aggregates, additives and polymer modified
    - Appearance and colour: Grey powder
    - Density: Fresh density of mortar ~2.0 kg/l
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: dmax: 0.4 mm
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.005 %
    - Compressive strength: Class R3; ~40 MPa after 56 days AS1012.9:2000
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ≥ 1.5 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Chloride ion diffusion resistance: 2.10E-11 (Nord Test 443) (m2/s)
    - Reaction to fire: Euro Class A1 (EN 1504-3)
2.7 Modulus of elasticity in compression.
    | ~ 20 GPa | (AS1012.17:2000) @ 56 days |
2.8 System structure. Sika MonoTop®-723 N is part of the range of Sika mortars complying with the relevant part of European Standard EN 1504 and comprising of: Bonding Primer / Reinforcement; Corrosion Protection
    | Sika MonoTop®-910 N | Normal Use |
    | SikaTop® Armatec® 110 EpoCem® | Demanding requirements |
    | Repair Mortar |
    | Sika MonoTop®-412, 352, Series | Concrete repair mortars |
    | Levelling Mortar |
    | Sika MonoTop®-723 N | Normal use |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.9 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bag
    - Shelf life: 12 months
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in undamaged original sealed packaging, in dry cool conditions.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment. The concrete shall be thoroughly clean, free from dust, loose material, surface contamination and materials which reduce bond or prevent suction or wetting by repair materials. Reference shall be made to EN1504-10 for specific requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: ~ 3.6-4.0 litres of water for 20 kg powder
    - Consumption: This depends on the substrate roughness and thickness of layer applied. As a guide, ~ 1.7 kg of powder per m² per mm thick
    - Yield: 20 kg yields approximately 11.7 litres of mortar
    - Layer thickness: min. 1 mm / max. 5 mm
    - Pot Life: ~40 minutes at 23°C
4.3 Waiting time to overcoating. As a guide, depending on weather conditions overcoat 4 days after application (3 days curing + 1 day drying) with Sikagard® range of protective coatings. For other emulsion paints, refer to the relevant manufacturer’s data sheet/ documentation.
4.4 Mixing.
    - Sika MonoTop®-723 N can be mixed with a low speed (<500 rpm) hand drill mixer or for machine application, using a force action mixer 2 to 3 bags or more at once depending the type and size of mixer. In small quantity, Sika MonoTop®-723 N can also be manually mixed.
    - Pour the recommended water in a suitable mixing container. While stirring slowly, add the powder to the water and mix thoroughly at least for 3 minutes to the required consistency.
4.5 Application.
    - Sika MonoTop®-723 N can be applied either manually using traditional techniques or mechanically using wet spray equipment. Thoroughly pre-wet the prepared substrate a recommended 2 hours before application. Keep the surface wet and do not allow to dry. Before application remove excess water e.g. with a clean sponge. The surface shall appear a dark matt appearance without glistening and surface pores and pits shall not contain water.
    - When manually applying the mortar first make a scratch coat by firmly scrapping the repair mortar over the substrate surface to form a thin layer and fill any pores or pits in the surface. The surface can be finished according to the requirements using a float or with a relevant wooden or plastic float or damp sponge.
4.6 Curing treatment. Protect the fresh mortar immediately from premature drying using an appropriate curing method e.g. moist geotextile membrane, polythene sheet etc.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be mechanically removed.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Refer to the Method Statement for Concrete Repair using Sika MonoTop® system for more information or refer to recommendations provided in EN 1504-10
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind.
    - Do not add water over recommended dosage
    - Apply only to sound prepared substrate, min 25 N/mm² compressive strength
    - Do not add additional water during the surface finishing as this will cause discolouration and cracking
    - Protect freshly applied material from freezing

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5°C minimum; +35°C maximum
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5°C minimum; +35°C maximum
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind.
    - Protect freshly applied material from freezing
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Class R3; ~40 MPa after 56 days AS1012.9:2000
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ≥ 1.5 MPa (EN 1542)
    - Chloride ion diffusion resistance: 2.10E-11 (Nord Test 443) (m2/s)
    - Reaction to fire: Euro Class A1 (EN 1504-3)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika MonoTop®-723 N, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/sika_monotop_-723n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika MonoTop®-723 N, version 27/10/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sds-sika-monotop-723n.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
